# v10.1.0

> Versioning reminder: the first segment matches the .NET major version, the second is a major library update, and the third is a minor update or patch. As a major library update, **10.1.0 contains breaking changes** — see [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes) and the [upgrade guide](#upgrade-guide) below.

**Release date:** TBD
**Minimum .NET version:** .NET 8.0
**Supported .NET versions:** .NET 8.0, .NET 9.0, .NET 10.0

---

## Highlights

- **Events now reach every handler.** Publishing an event previously invoked only the last registered handler.
- **Registering modules more than once is safe.** Scanning several assemblies no longer runs pre/post handlers multiple times.
- **Separate lifetimes for the mediator and its handlers** via `MediatorLifetime` and `HandlerLifetime`.
- **Mock `SendAsync` and `PublishAsync` directly.** `SendAsync` is now an `IMediator` member instead of an extension method.
- **5–13% faster dispatch** for commands, queries and events.

---

## Bug fixes

### Events invoked only one handler

`IPublisher.PublishAsync` resolved a single `IEventHandler<TEvent>`, so when an event had several handlers only the last registered one ran; the others were skipped without any error.

All registered handlers now run, **sequentially in registration order**. Pre- and post-handlers still run once per publish.

### Publishing an event with no handlers threw

Publishing an event that nobody handles used to throw `InvalidOperationException`. It is now a **no-op**, which is the usual publish/subscribe behavior.

### Calling `AddCommands` / `AddQueries` / `AddEvents` more than once duplicated behaviors

Each call re-registered the built-in pre/post-handler pipeline behaviors. Scanning three assemblies made every pre- and post-handler run six times.

Registration is now idempotent: handlers, built-in behaviors, your own pipeline behaviors and `IPublisher` are each registered once, however many times the configuration methods are called and whichever assemblies they scan.

### Assembly scanning robustness

- Assemblies containing types that fail to load (for example, because an optional dependency is missing) are scanned instead of failing with `ReflectionTypeLoadException`.
- Open-generic handler classes (such as `LoggingPreHandler<T>`) are skipped instead of being registered as unusable services.

---

## New features

### Separate mediator and handler lifetimes

`ArcanicMediatorConfiguration` has two new properties:

| Property | Applies to | Default |
|----------|------------|---------|
| `MediatorLifetime` | `IMediator`, `IPublisher` | `Transient` |
| `HandlerLifetime` | handlers, pre/post handlers, pipeline behaviors | `Transient` |

```csharp
builder.Services.AddArcanicMediator(config =>
{
    config.MediatorLifetime = InstanceLifetime.Scoped;
    config.HandlerLifetime = InstanceLifetime.Scoped;
})
.AddCommands(Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly());
```

A `Singleton` mediator combined with `Scoped` handlers would resolve scoped handlers from the root provider, so that combination is now rejected at startup with an `InvalidOperationException`.

### Mockable `SendAsync`

`SendAsync` is now declared on `IMediator` itself instead of being an extension method, so it can be mocked and verified directly with Moq, NSubstitute or any other mocking library — just like `IPublisher.PublishAsync`:

```csharp
public interface IMediator
{
    Task<TResponse> SendAsync<TResponse>(IRequest<TResponse> request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    Task SendAsync(IRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
```

```csharp
var mediator = new Mock<IMediator>();
mediator
    .Setup(m => m.SendAsync(It.IsAny<GetProductQuery>(), It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()))
    .ReturnsAsync(new ProductDto(1, "Test", 9.99m));
```

A new `IRequest<TResponse>` interface, implemented by `ICommand<T>` and `IQuery<T>`, lets the compiler infer the response type, so existing calls such as `await mediator.SendAsync(command)` compile unchanged.

Requests that no registered module can handle now fail with a message naming the request type and pointing to `AddCommands` / `AddQueries`.

## Breaking changes

| Change | Who is affected |
|--------|-----------------|
| Publishing an event with no handlers no longer throws `InvalidOperationException` | Code that relied on that exception |
| `IMediator.ServiceProvider` and `IMediator.RequestDispatchers` removed; `IMediator` now declares the two `SendAsync` methods | Code that implemented `IMediator`, or read those members |
| `ICommand<T>` and `IQuery<T>` now also implement the new `IRequest<T>` | No action needed; listed for completeness |
| `RequestDispatcherBase` moved from `Arcanic.Mediator.Request.Abstractions` (namespace `Arcanic.Mediator.Request.Abstractions.Dispatcher`) to `Arcanic.Mediator.Request` (namespace `Arcanic.Mediator.Request.Dispatcher`) | Code that subclassed or referenced it |
| Protected `GetAllPipelineBehaviors` removed from `CommandDispatcherBase`, `QueryDispatcherBase` and `EventDispatcherBase` | Code that subclassed the dispatchers |
| `IServiceRegistrar` gained `TryRegister(Type, Type)`, `TryRegister(Type, Type, InstanceLifetime)` and `Configuration` | Custom implementations of `IServiceRegistrar` |
| The `MediatorExtensions` classes (Command and Query packages) are removed; `SendAsync` is an `IMediator` member | Code calling `MediatorExtensions.SendAsync(...)` as a static method |
| `IPublisher.PublishAsync` parameter renamed from `request` to `@event` | Callers using the named argument `request:` |
| `ArcanicMediatorConfiguration.InstanceLifetime` is obsolete | Produces a compiler warning; behavior is unchanged |

Calls such as `mediator.SendAsync(command)`, `mediator.SendAsync(query)` and `publisher.PublishAsync(@event)` compile and behave exactly as before.

---

## Upgrade guide

1. **Lifetimes.** Replace `config.InstanceLifetime = X;` with:
   ```csharp
   config.MediatorLifetime = X;
   config.HandlerLifetime = X;
   ```
   The obsolete property still sets both, so this step only removes the compiler warning.
2. **Events with several handlers.** Check that every handler is meant to run. Before this release only the last registered handler ran, so a handler that was silently skipped will now execute.
3. **Events without handlers.** Remove any code that catches `InvalidOperationException` to detect an event without subscribers.
4. **Custom `IMediator` implementations.** Implement the two `SendAsync` methods instead of `ServiceProvider` and `RequestDispatchers`. Mocks can now set up `SendAsync` directly.
5. **Custom `IServiceRegistrar` implementations.** Add the two `TryRegister` overloads and the `Configuration` property.
6. **Namespace update.** Replace `using Arcanic.Mediator.Request.Abstractions.Dispatcher;` with `using Arcanic.Mediator.Request.Dispatcher;` if you reference `RequestDispatcherBase`.

---

## Improvements

### Performance

Pipeline composition no longer builds a LINQ chain on every dispatch. Measured with the repository benchmarks (BenchmarkDotNet in-process job, .NET 10), compared with v10.0.0:

| Benchmark | v10.0.0 | v10.1.0 |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| Command `CreateUser` | 351.6 ns | 342.9 ns |
| Command `UpdateUser` | 396.3 ns | 318.8 ns |
| Command `DeleteUser` | 326.9 ns | 285.2 ns |
| Query `GetUser` | 443.0 ns | 411.2 ns |
| Query `SearchUsers` | 393.0 ns | 351.5 ns |
| Event `UserCreatedEvent` | 435.9 ns / 856 B | 367.3 ns / 824 B |
| Event `UserDeletedEvent` | 372.1 ns / 816 B | 349.6 ns / 784 B |
| Event `UserUpdatedEvent` | 332.3 ns / 840 B | 340.7 ns / 808 B |

Allocations for commands and queries are unchanged; events allocate 32 B less per publish. `UserUpdatedEvent` timing is within measurement noise.

### Lighter dependencies

- `Arcanic.Mediator` depends only on `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions` instead of the full `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` container package.
- The `*.Abstractions` packages no longer carry any DI dependency.

### Internal cleanup

Assembly scanning, pipeline-behavior validation, pre/post-handler behaviors and pipeline composition were duplicated across the Command, Query and Event modules. Each now exists once in `Arcanic.Mediator`. The module pre/post behaviors derive from the new public `PreHandlerPipelineBehaviorBase` and `PostHandlerPipelineBehaviorBase` classes.

`SendAsync` and `PublishAsync` now use `ConfigureAwait(false)` throughout.

---

## Infrastructure and documentation

- **Release workflow:** uses `gh release create` instead of the archived `actions/create-release`; only releases commits on `main`; builds the package list from the packed files; declares explicit token permissions.
- **Packaging:** `GeneratePackageOnBuild` is disabled; packages are produced by `dotnet pack`. Every package's release notes now link to the GitHub releases page, and the `Request` packages have accurate descriptions and tags.
- **Tests:** 31 → 84 tests per target framework, covering multi-handler events, repeated registration, pipeline-behavior validation, every lifetime combination and `IMediator` dispatch. The test suite moved from FluentAssertions (commercial license from v8) to [AwesomeAssertions](https://github.com/AwesomeAssertions/AwesomeAssertions) (MIT).
- **README:** event handlers are documented as sequential (not parallel), the lifetime options are documented, and a testing section shows how to mock `IMediator` and `IPublisher` with Moq and NSubstitute.
